description: Milk powder spray dryer (main air chamber, static and vibrating fluid beds, exhaust air with heat recovery). Loads in kW. Table 1 data as published.
reference: Walmsley, Lincoln, Padullés, Cleland (2024), Energies 17, 2838, Table 1 (case first presented by Liang et al.).

HTHP 200 °C (main air): lift 185 K above 130 K: beyond reported COP data

provenance.stream data: published (Table 1). WARNING: Table 1 is inconsistent with the paper's own targets (4.98 / 3.99 MW) by the first law; see verify_walmsley2024.py
provenance.source_T_C: assumed: 15 °C (dead state), where the cooled exhaust air ends
provenance.sink levels: assumed, illustrative: 120 °C (fluid beds) and 200 °C (upper end of IEA HPT Annex 58 scope); the main air chamber up to 236 °C stays on fired heating
provenance.basis: published: 6000 h/year, Liang et al. (2022), 'Full electrification opportunities of spray dryers in milk powder processes', ECOS 2022, Copenhagen (DTU accepted manuscript, peer-reviewed): the source of the stream data in Walmsley et al. (2024) Table 1 (GEA Process Engineering, skim milk powder dryer), Sec. 2.1
provenance.economics: assumed: no economic data in the source (see economics.sources)
provenance.film coefficients: Liang et al. (2022), Table 2 (from Zühlsdorf et al.): overall U water-air 42.5 W/(m2 K) on the air-side area. Air-air heat transfer is done through water loops (direct air-air exchange is not used in practice, Sec. 2.1), i.e. two water-air exchangers in series: h = 0.0425 kW/(m2 K) per air stream gives U = 21 W/(m2 K) per match
provenance.eta_lorenz_sensitivity: 0.45-0.52: Lorenz (Carnot) efficiencies implied by the DEA catalogue HTHP sheets 2.a/2.b (COP 4.45/2.75/2.4/2.05 at lifts of 40/65/80/100 K), as for the brewery
provenance.COP check: HTHP 120 °C (105 K lift): COP 1.87 vs DEA sheet 2.a about 1.96 at 105 K (-4.6 %, conservative). HTHP 200 °C: COP 1.28 from a 15 °C source; Liang et al. (2022) use the exhaust (via water loops) as source and reach COP 2.61 for the steam heat pump, Liang et al. (2023, IIR ICR) a total COP of 2.68 with a transcritical CO2 cycle: the illustrative isothermal design here is pessimistic

default_sources.electricity_to_gas_ratio: published: Padullés et al. (2026), Sec. 5.2, 'current European ratios of around 2'
default_sources.boiler_efficiency: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat, sheet 6.1 'Boiler, gas and oil' (2025): total efficiency, net, annual average 93.9 % (range 91.9-94.9 %), steam boiler with economiser; converted to the gross (GCV) basis of Eurostat gas prices with NCV/GCV = 0.90: 0.939 x 0.90 = 0.845. Earlier default 0.817 (US DOE Steam Tip Sheet #15, HHV) kept as sensitivity
default_sources.payback_threshold_years: research question 1 (industry practice 3-5 years: Cooremans, cited in Padullés et al. 2026)
default_sources.gas_EF_kg_per_kWh: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Vol. 2, Ch. 2, Table 2.2: natural gas, stationary combustion, 56,100 kg CO2/TJ (NCV) = 0.202 kg/kWh NCV = 0.182 kg/kWh GCV (NCV/GCV = 0.90), direct combustion only, matching the scope of production-based grid factors. Padullés et al. (2026, Sec. 5.3) use 0.219 (scope not stated); report it as a sensitivity
default_sources.grid_EF_kg_per_kWh: APA, 'Fator de Emissão da Eletricidade - 2025', Table T1: Portugal 2023, 0.107 t CO2eq/MWh (annual, production-based, direct emissions). Sensitivities: mainland 2023 0.092; 5-year moving average 0.167 (Table T2); Electricity Maps 2025 flow-traced 0.1172
default_sources.co2_price_EUR_per_t: 0 by default (site may be outside the EU ETS); sensitivity uses the EUA price
default_sources.pef_gas: convention: primary energy of a fuel = its final energy
default_sources.refrigeration_credit_fraction: share of the refrigeration that the heat pump sources can take over that is actually credited (1 = all, continuous operation as in Padullés et al. 2026 Sec. 5.1; lower values represent batch mismatch between heat pump and cooling loads)
default_sources.chiller_cop: no refrigeration credit unless set (Padullés et al. 2026 do not count it). Sinnott and Towler (2020), Sec. 6.4.4: real COP about 0.6 x Carnot for a simple cycle (up to 0.9 for complex cycles)

case_sources.prices: Eurostat nrg_pc_203 (gas) and nrg_pc_205 (electricity), Portugal, 2026-S1, excluding VAT and other recoverable taxes and levies, EUR/kWh, gas on GCV (data/sources/eurostat_portugal_prices.csv). The plant is not in Portugal: these prices place it in the dissertation's context. Bands at the published 6000 h/year: powder rate not published (air flows only: main air 77,762 kg/h, Liang et al. 2022 Table 1); estimated 8.3 t/h from the air heating (6.03 MW) and 2,610 MJ/t air-heater use (Walmsley et al. 2016, CET 52). Gas 5.2 GJ/t x 8.3 x 6000 = 0.26 million GJ (I4, 0.0445); electricity 220 kWh/t x 8.3 x 6000 = 11 GWh + heat pumps 14.7 GWh = 26 GWh (IE, 0.0897). Both bands hold for any plant between 4 and 32 t/h, so the estimate does not change the prices
case_sources.heat_pump_cost: Danish Energy Agency catalogue (2025) by sink temperature, linear in capacity, plus the catalogue's add-ons for lift above 75 K (sink outlet minus source outlet) and steam generation (isothermal sinks). Replaces Padullés et al. (2026, Table 3), which is fitted to brewery heat pumps and gives 0.75-0.88 M€/MW for 2-3 MW units, below the catalogue range 0.9-1.5 M€/MW for sinks up to 125 °C. Indirect cost of new hot-water piping (0.23 M€/MW, 'relevant when needing to install new hot water piping instead of existing steam piping') is a scenario, not in the base. Steam add-on only for the 200 °C level: in Liang et al. (2022), 'Full electrification opportunities of spray dryers in milk powder processes', ECOS 2022, Copenhagen (DTU accepted manuscript, peer-reviewed): the source of the stream data in Walmsley et al. (2024) Table 1 (GEA Process Engineering, skim milk powder dryer) the existing dryer heats air with steam heaters from a steam boiler (Fig. 1, Sec. 2.4); in the electrified design the NH3 and hydrocarbon heat pumps deliver hot-water loops (water loops avoid product contamination, Sec. 2.1) and only the top unit is a closed-loop steam heat pump
case_sources.comparison: Liang et al. (2022), 5 %/20 y, 6000 h, renewable electricity 40 €/MWh, Danish gas 31 €/MWh incl. taxes, boiler 0.9: full electrification (NH3 + hydrocarbon + steam heat pumps, water loops, > 12,000 m2 of air-water exchangers) TCI 8.1-8.4 M€, levelised cost of heat 35.1-36.2 €/MWh vs 35.8 for the gas boiler; steam heat pump COP 2.61 (Lorenz efficiency 33 %), other heat pumps COP > 2

heat_pump_cost_class.HTHP 200 °C (main air): hp_dea_2b + dea_lift_2b + dea_steam (extrapolated: sink above every class)

RQ1._definition: fraction = heat pump heat / Q̇h,min of the site with heat recovery installed

retrofit_bounds.baseline_meaning: the source states that the plant has no heat recovery: this baseline is the real plant
retrofit_bounds.note: Liang et al. (2022), Sec. 2.1 and Fig. 1: in the standard installation the inlet air is not heated by the exhaust (no air-to-air exchange), every air stream is heated by steam heaters and the exhaust is vented. Their electrified design recovers exhaust heat through water loops, which the film coefficients here represent (two water-air exchangers per match). The new-network cost uses the sweep (no verified air-water exchanger cost law)

new_heat_recovery_network.cost_law: 100 €/m² installed (not a cost estimate: Liang et al. (2022) Table 3 fin-and-tube fit gives about 72 per m2 at 756 m2 per unit on a 1998 basis (currency and escalation not verified); costs have risen since. 100 €/m2 also gives dTmin,opt 8 K in step 3, the approach of Liang's minimum cost of heat)

options.option: New heat recovery at target + heat pumps
Lower bound: plant already at target, heat pumps only

assumptions.new network: area target (Bath formula, case film coefficients) and units target at the case's temperature shifts, costed per unit with the cost law
assumptions.heat pumps: case sink levels; on the no-recovery plant they are sized on the network-constrained stream set (no process-to-process transfer)

area_targeting.film_coefficients_source: Liang et al. (2022), Table 2 (from Zühlsdorf et al.): overall U water-air 42.5 W/(m2 K) on the air-side area. Air-air heat transfer is done through water loops (direct air-air exchange is not used in practice, Sec. 2.1), i.e. two water-air exchangers in series: h = 0.0425 kW/(m2 K) per air stream gives U = 21 W/(m2 K) per match
